reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Every English line of the chapter was read against the Greek. No line adds interpretive content, uses Raëlian-canon vocabulary (no Elohim, Yahweh, craft, creators, ray, planet, Eternals), or resolves an ambiguity in the canon's direction. Each Wheel of Heaven reading sits in its own paragraph headed 'reception note, not a translation claim'. The two lines that coincide with the canon's French were tested specifically: 2:2/2:9 'at its rising' (BDAG ἀνατολή 1 cites both verses; NAB 1970, NRSV, ESV) and 26:53 'put at my disposal' (BDAG παρίστημι 1a cites the verse; NASB identical wording). In both the lexical ground is real and independent of the canon, so neither is lens leakage.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts were formed from the Greek, the chapter JSON, the overlay and the central diff before the escalation report (wave-m2-editor-report.md) was opened. The report added no information that changes a verdict. It repeats the RSV attribution for 2:2/9 ('RSV, NRSV, NAB'), which this review corrects. Its ten founder-preference points are answered in founderDecisionRecommendations, and its follow-ups (17:21; 17:22; comma/colon in 25 and 28; the 6:13 'testing' wording in central) are endorsed as later-pass items.

founderDecisionRecommendations.1-angelos-angel: Endorse. ἄγγελος is the technical term for a heavenly envoy in first-century Jewish Greek (BDAG s.v. 2); published Mt 1, 13, 25, 28, Acts 12 and the Revelation wave all print 'angel', so the Greek NT is already harmonized in practice. Promote jointly with Revelation as a central Greek-NT convention; keep 'messenger of YHWH' for Hebrew malʾāḵ.
founderDecisionRecommendations.2-naos-sanctuary: Endorse for Matthew. The naos/hieron distinction is lexical (BDAG; Josephus) and NRSV marks it in 23:16-35. 27:5 keeps Matthew's crux honestly (and, to my reading, restores the ASV's own 'sanctuary'). If promoted, scope it to books with both terms; Revelation's 'temple' for ναός is defensible because it has no ἱερόν.
founderDecisionRecommendations.3-23:14-no-paragraph: Endorse. SBLGNT has no 23:14; the Byzantine text is quoted in full at 23:13 with witnesses, as the 6:13b precedent and the Revelation ruling C require. Recommend a later pass bring the stable 17:21 into line: its bracketed Greek is not SBLGNT text, so drop the paragraph and move the Byzantine wording into the 17:20 commentary.
founderDecisionRecommendations.4-colon-convention: Endorse (punctuation only; applied without exception in the wave). Harmonize published 25 and 28 in a later pass.
founderDecisionRecommendations.5-magi: Endorse. 'magi' is the standard scholarly rendering (BDAG; Brown; Powell) and NIV/NAB usage; 'wise men' is noted.
founderDecisionRecommendations.6-faithfulness-23:23: Endorse. BDAG lists Mt 23:23 under πίστις 1a 'faithfulness, reliability'; NIV and ESV render so; the Mic 6:8 triad is conduct.
founderDecisionRecommendations.7-put-at-my-disposal-26:53: Endorse. BDAG παρίστημι 1a cites this verse for 'put at someone's disposal', and the NASB prints exactly 'put at My disposal'; the ground is independent of the canon's French, and the coincidence is disclosed.
founderDecisionRecommendations.8-at-its-rising-2:2,9: Endorse. BDAG ἀνατολή 1 cites both verses; NAB (1970, before TBWTT) and NRSV read 'at its rising', ESV 'when it rose'. Correct the RSV attribution (the RSV reads 'in the East').
founderDecisionRecommendations.9-defiles-a-person: Endorse. The article with ἄνθρωπος is generic; the canon's own French « l'homme » is generic too, so the line follows the sense the canon intends rather than the English edition's 'the man'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.10-tempted-4:1: Endorse. Agent-driven 'tempted'/'the tempter' is BDAG's and the versions' reading with the devil as agent, and agrees with published 6:13; the test reading (Gerhardsson; canon « mis à l'épreuve ») is properly in commentary. Optionally align the chapter 4 title ('The testing in the wilderness') with the line.

paragraphs.text: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις παραγίνεται Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς κηρύσσων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῆς Ἰουδαίας
paragraphs.translit: en de tais hēmerais ekeinais paraginetai iōannēs ho baptistēs kēryssōn en tē erēmō tēs ioudaias

i18n.en: Now in those days John the Baptist comes, preaching in the wilderness of Judea

notes.official: *paraginetai* 'comes' is a historic present, kept. *ho baptistēs* 'the Baptist' is a title, 'the baptizer'.

paragraphs.text: καὶ λέγων· Μετανοεῖτε, ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai legōn· metanoeite, ēngiken gar hē basileia tōn ouranōn.

i18n.en: and saying: "Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has come near."

notes.official: *metanoeite* 'Repent', literally 'change your mind'. *ēngiken* is a perfect, 'has come near' (ASV 'is at hand'). John's proclamation is word for word that of Jesus at 4:17 and of the disciples at 10:7. 'The kingdom of the heavens' keeps Matthew's plural (`kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim`).

paragraphs.text: οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ῥηθεὶς διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: houtos gar estin ho rhētheis dia ēsaiou tou prophētou legontos· phōnē boōntos en tē erēmō· hetoimasate tēn hodon kyriou, eutheias poieite tas tribous autou.

i18n.en: For this is the one who was spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying: "The voice of one crying in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.'"

notes.official: Isa 40:3 LXX. In the Hebrew 'in the wilderness' belongs to 'prepare' ('In the wilderness prepare the way of YHWH'); the LXX, followed by Matthew, attaches it to 'crying', which fits John's preaching 'in the wilderness' (3:1). *kyrios* 'the Lord' stands for the Hebrew YHWH, and Matthew writes 'his paths' where the LXX has 'the paths of our God'. In Greek quotations the program keeps *kyrios* as 'the Lord'.

paragraphs.text: αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Ἰωάννης εἶχεν τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τριχῶν καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ, ἡ δὲ τροφὴ ἦν αὐτοῦ ἀκρίδες καὶ μέλι ἄγριον.
paragraphs.translit: autos de ho iōannēs eichen to endyma autou apo trichōn kamēlou kai zōnēn dermatinēn peri tēn osphyn autou, hē de trophē ēn autou akrides kai meli agrion.

i18n.en: Now John himself had his garment of camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.

notes.official: The garment of camel's hair and the leather belt recall Elijah's description in 2 Kgs 1:8 ('a hairy man, with a girdle of leather about his loins'); Matthew identifies John with Elijah at 11:14 and 17:12-13.

paragraphs.text: τότε ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία καὶ πᾶσα ἡ περίχωρος τοῦ Ἰορδάνου,
paragraphs.translit: tote exeporeueto pros auton hierosolyma kai pasa hē ioudaia kai pasa hē perichōros tou iordanou,

i18n.en: Then Jerusalem and all Judea and all the region around the Jordan were going out to him,

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ebaptizonto en tō iordanē potamō hypʼ autou exomologoumenoi tas hamartias autōn.

i18n.en: and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.

paragraphs.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ πολλοὺς τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων ἐρχομένους ἐπὶ τὸ βάπτισμα αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, τίς ὑπέδειξεν ὑμῖν φυγεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς μελλούσης ὀργῆς;
paragraphs.translit: idōn de pollous tōn pharisaiōn kai saddoukaiōn erchomenous epi to baptisma autou eipen autois· gennēmata echidnōn, tis hypedeixen hymin phygein apo tēs mellousēs orgēs;

i18n.en: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them: "Offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

notes.official: *gennēmata echidnōn* 'offspring of vipers' (ASV 'Ye offspring of vipers'), used again by Jesus at 12:34 and 23:33.

paragraphs.text: ποιήσατε οὖν καρπὸν ἄξιον τῆς μετανοίας
paragraphs.translit: poiēsate oun karpon axion tēs metanoias

i18n.en: Bear therefore fruit worthy of repentance;

paragraphs.text: καὶ μὴ δόξητε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ, λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι δύναται ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν λίθων τούτων ἐγεῖραι τέκνα τῷ Ἀβραάμ.
paragraphs.translit: kai mē doxēte legein en heautois· patera echomen ton abraam, legō gar hymin hoti dynatai ho theos ek tōn lithōn toutōn egeirai tekna tō abraam.

i18n.en: and do not presume to say within yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father'; for I say to you that God is able from these stones to raise up children to Abraham.

notes.official: 'from these stones to raise up children to Abraham': many commentators suspect an Aramaic wordplay behind the Greek, *ʾaḇnayyāʾ* 'stones' and *bənayyāʾ* 'children' (Davies and Allison, ICC, ad loc.).

paragraphs.text: ἤδη δὲ ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται· πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
paragraphs.translit: ēdē de hē axinē pros tēn rhizan tōn dendrōn keitai· pan oun dendron mē poioun karpon kalon ekkoptetai kai eis pyr balletai.

i18n.en: And already the axe is laid at the root of the trees; every tree therefore that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

paragraphs.text: Ἐγὼ μὲν ὑμᾶς βαπτίζω ἐν ὕδατι εἰς μετάνοιαν· ὁ δὲ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἰσχυρότερός μού ἐστιν, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς τὰ ὑποδήματα βαστάσαι· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί·
paragraphs.translit: egō men hymas baptizō en hydati eis metanoian· ho de opisō mou erchomenos ischyroteros mou estin, hou ouk eimi hikanos ta hypodēmata bastasai· autos hymas baptisei en pneumati hagiō kai pyri·

i18n.en: I indeed baptize you in water for repentance; but he who is coming after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry; he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.

notes.official: *en pneumati hagiō kai pyri* 'in the Holy Spirit and fire': *en* is kept as 'in', matching 'in water' in the same verse. 'Holy Spirit' is capitalized as in the published 1:18, 20 and 28:19 (`pneuma-spirit-capitalization-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ συνάξει τὸν σῖτον αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ.
paragraphs.translit: hou to ptyon en tē cheiri autou, kai diakathariei tēn halōna autou kai synaxei ton siton autou eis tēn apothēkēn, to de achyron katakausei pyri asbestō.

i18n.en: His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will thoroughly clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn up with unquenchable fire."

paragraphs.text: Τότε παραγίνεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰορδάνην πρὸς τὸν Ἰωάννην τοῦ βαπτισθῆναι ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: tote paraginetai ho iēsous apo tēs galilaias epi ton iordanēn pros ton iōannēn tou baptisthēnai hypʼ autou.

i18n.en: Then Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰωάννης διεκώλυεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἐγὼ χρείαν ἔχω ὑπὸ σοῦ βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ σὺ ἔρχῃ πρός με;
paragraphs.translit: ho de iōannēs diekōlyen auton legōn· egō chreian echō hypo sou baptisthēnai, kai sy erchē pros me;

i18n.en: But John would have prevented him, saying: "I have need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?"

paragraphs.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἄφες ἄρτι, οὕτως γὰρ πρέπον ἐστὶν ἡμῖν πληρῶσαι πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην. τότε ἀφίησιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho iēsous eipen pros auton· aphes arti, houtōs gar prepon estin hēmin plērōsai pasan dikaiosynēn. tote aphiēsin auton.

i18n.en: But Jesus answered and said to him: "Permit it now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness." Then he permits him.

notes.official: *plērōsai pasan dikaiosynēn* 'to fulfill all righteousness': the first use of *dikaiosynē* in Matthew, a key word of the Sermon (5:6, 10, 20; 6:1, 33). *aphiēsin auton* 'he permits him' is a historic present.

paragraphs.text: βαπτισθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εὐθὺς ἀνέβη ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕδατος· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἠνεῴχθησαν οἱ οὐρανοί, καὶ εἶδεν πνεῦμα θεοῦ καταβαῖνον ὡσεὶ περιστερὰν ἐρχόμενον ἐπʼ αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: baptistheis de ho iēsous euthys anebē apo tou hydatos· kai idou ēneōchthēsan hoi ouranoi, kai eiden pneuma theou katabainon hōsei peristeran erchomenon epʼ auton·

i18n.en: And when Jesus had been baptized, he went up immediately from the water; and behold, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him;

notes.official:
*ēneōchthēsan hoi ouranoi* 'the heavens were opened': SBLGNT has no *autō*. NA28 prints [*autō*] in brackets, and the Byzantine text and the KJV include it ('opened unto him'); Vaticanus (first hand) and Sinaiticus (first hand) lack it (`critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`). The phrase recalls Ezek 1:1 LXX (*ēnoichthēsan hoi ouranoi*) and Isa 63:19 (EV 64:1), 'Oh that you would tear open the heavens and come down'.

*pneuma theou* 'the Spirit of God': the anarthrous head noun is definite through the following genitive, as the arthrous *hypo tou pneumatos* in 4:1 confirms, and is capitalized as in 1:18 (`pneuma-spirit-capitalization-matthew`). *hōsei peristeran* 'like a dove' can describe the manner of descent or the visible form; Luke 3:22 takes it as form ('in bodily form').

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 4) quotes 3:16-17 with 4:1 (« les cieux s'ouvrirent ; il vit l'Esprit de Dieu descendre comme une colombe et venir sur lui … ») as the moment when, having reached adulthood, Jesus is taken by the creators to be shown his Father and his mission and to be initiated in scientific techniques. The canon's French reads, as the critical text does, without 'to him'. The line renders the Greek and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou phōnē ek tōn ouranōn legousa· houtos estin ho huios mou ho agapētos, en hō eudokēsa.

i18n.en: and behold, a voice from the heavens, saying: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."

notes.official:
*houtos estin ho huios mou ho agapētos, en hō eudokēsa* 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased': the voice combines Ps 2:7 ('You are my son') and Isa 42:1 ('my chosen, in whom my soul delights'). Matthew's 'This is' is a public declaration; Mark 1:11 and Luke 3:22 have 'You are'. The second article (*ho agapētos*) allows the appositional 'my Son, the beloved', which is how the canon's French reads it. 'My beloved Son' is the standard rendering of the attributive construction and is kept to agree with the published 17:5, where the Greek is the same (`huios-theou-son-of-god-rendering-matthew`). *ek tōn ouranōn* 'from the heavens' keeps the plural.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 4) quotes the voice as « Celui-ci est mon fils, l'aimé dont je suis content » (EN 'This is my son, the beloved in whom I am well pleased'), and reads it as the presentation of Jesus to his Father among the creators. The appositional wording is a legitimate construal of the Greek and is documented here; the line keeps the form used at 17:5.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual variant: SBLGNT reads ἠνεῴχθησαν οἱ οὐρανοί without αὐτῷ; NA28 prints [αὐτῷ] in brackets, and the Byzantine/TR text (KJV 'the heavens were opened unto him') includes it. The canon (TBWTT ch. 4) quotes « les cieux s'ouvrirent » without 'to him'. Draft follows SBLGNT.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: SBLGNT followed (no 'to him'); NA28 bracket and Byzantine/KJV reading recorded; canon quotes without 'to him'.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: πνεῦμα θεοῦ (pneuma theou, anarthrous; also τοῦ πνεύματος at 4:1, πνεύματι ἁγίῳ at 3:11): capitalization and article on the English surface are unglossed. The canon quotes « l'Esprit de Dieu ».
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'the Spirit of God', capitalized with article, consistent with published 'Holy Spirit' (1:18, 20; 28:19); lower case for human spirit and unclean spirits; Gen 1:2 'breath of Elohim' not applied.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Canon-wording difference: Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός is quoted in TBWTT ch. 4 as « Celui-ci est mon fils, l'aimé » ('my son, the beloved'). Draft keeps the precedent rendering at 17:5 ('my beloved Son'); the Greek's second article (ὁ ἀγαπητός) admits the appositional reading.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'This is my beloved Son' kept, matching published 17:5 (same Greek); appositional 'my Son, the beloved' (canon) documented in commentary and reception note.
